title: A holistic computational exploration of AZD7762 as a potent selective modulator of LXRalpha, LXRbeta and FXR: An underexplored pathway in cancer therapeutics.
authors: Singha, Basanta; Gogoi, Partha Pratim; Longkumer, Penlisola; Ahmed, Benzir; Boruah, Nichan; Bezbaruah, Bipul; Sinha, Upasana Bora
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过虚拟筛选、分子对接和分子动力学模拟探索AZD7762对核受体LXR/FXR的调控，对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of global mortality, necessitating novel therapeutic strategies. Liver X Receptors (LXRalpha and LXRbeta) and the Farnesoid X Receptor (FXR) are nuclear receptors that regulate lipid and cholesterol homeostasis, bile acid metabolism, inflammation, and immune response pathways intricately linked to cellular dysregulation in oncogenesis. Despite their therapeutic potential, these receptors remain underexplored targets in cancer research. This study implements an extensive suite of computational strategies to identify and evaluate potential modulators of LXRalpha/beta and FXR, through virtual screening using resveratrol as the lead scaffold, followed by drug-likeness evaluation and toxicity profiling. Molecular docking (MVD, AutoDock and ML-PLIC) identified C144 (AZD7762), a well-established CHK1 kinase inhibitor, as the top-ranked ligand, demonstrating superior binding affinity and conformational stability via convergent interaction mechanisms. Additionally, reactivity descriptors derived from density functional theory (DFT) and frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analyses further substantiated its favorable electronic properties and chemical stability. Structural pharmacophore mapping using LigandScout confirmed pharmacophoric alignment with receptor active sites, while bioactivity profiles predicted high efficacy. Extensive quantum mechanical analyses (MEP, NBO, Mulliken/NPA, NCI, RDG, ELF, LOL, BSA, HAS) revealed favorable electronic characteristics, stability, charge distribution, and interaction potential. CLC-Pred, biotransformation (RA), pharmacokinetic profiling, molecular dynamics simulations, MM/PBSA and Shermo-based thermodynamic predictions further validated its biostability and systemic compatibility. These findings position C144 (AZD7762) as a promising anticancer candidate targeting LXRalpha, LXRbeta, and FXR pathways. Further optimization and validation through in vitro and in vivo studies are essential for advancing these findings toward clinical application.
abstract_zh: 癌症仍然是全球死亡的主要原因之一，亟需新的治疗策略。肝X受体（LXRalpha和LXRbeta）和法尼醇X受体（FXR）是核受体，调节脂质和胆固醇稳态、胆汁酸代谢、炎症及免疫反应通路，这些通路与肿瘤发生中的细胞失调密切相关。尽管具有治疗潜力，这些受体在癌症研究中仍是未被充分探索的靶点。本研究采用一套广泛的计算策略，通过以白藜芦醇为先导骨架的虚拟筛选，识别并评估LXRalpha/beta和FXR的潜在调节剂，随后进行药物相似性评估和毒性分析。分子对接（MVD、AutoDock和ML-PLIC）将C144（AZD7762），一种公认的CHK1激酶抑制剂，鉴定为排名最高的配体，通过趋同的相互作用机制表现出优异的结合亲和力和构象稳定性。此外，基于密度泛函理论（DFT）和前沿分子轨道（FMO）分析的反应性描述符进一步证实了其有利的电子性质和化学稳定性。使用LigandScout进行的结构药效团映射确认了与受体活性位点的药效团对齐，而生物活性谱预测了高效力。广泛的量子力学分析（MEP、NBO、Mulliken/NPA、NCI、RDG、ELF、LOL、BSA、HAS）揭示了有利的电子特性、稳定性、电荷分布和相互作用潜力。CLC-Pred、生物转化（RA）、药代动力学分析、分子动力学模拟、MM/PBSA和基于Shermo的热力学预测进一步验证了其生物稳定性和系统兼容性。这些发现将C144（AZD7762）定位为靶向LXRalpha、LXRbeta和FXR通路的有前景的抗癌候选药物。通过体外和体内研究的进一步优化和验证对于将这些发现推进至临床应用至关重要。
